title: Astrid and the Lantern
premise: In 1911, in a fog-bound Baltic port city, Bram Montrose lives as a young man to work as an apprentice clockmaker, hiding both her sex and her past in the free city's cracks. When census taker Astrid Lindqvist arrives with inconvenient questions, she uncovers Bram's secret but keeps it—because years ago, in peacetime, Bram promised Astrid's brother Emil, now declared an enemy national facing deportation, that she would get him out when the time came. As war rumors harden into law and the observatory's master clock becomes the city's official timekeeper for curfews and troop movements, Bram must sabotage her own masterpiece of repair to buy Emil one night of escape—with Astrid as reluctant accomplice, torn between duty and loyalty. The novel ends with the clock stopped at midnight, Emil gone on a northbound coal barge, Bram unmasked before the guild but defended by Astrid's testimony, and the two women beginning an uneasy, honest life together as keepers of the clock.
about_author: Mara Underhill is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging port-city municipal records from the early twentieth century. She writes historical fiction about people history filed under the wrong name.

chapters.title: The Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Establishes her careful double life at Hessler & Sons clockworks: binding her chest, keeping hands busy, answering to 'boy.' The census taker Astrid arrives at the workshop and asks where Bram was born—a question with no safe answer. Emotional beat: the first crack in invisibility, dread beneath competence.

chapters.title: Twelve Bells, One Lie
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Summoned to repair the observatory's master clock, Bram climbs into its works and finds a kind of peace only gears understand. Astrid appears again, officially verifying the census; privately she reveals she knows 'Bram' was born Birgitta. Emotional beat: exposure without betrayal—the terrifying mercy of being seen.

chapters.title: What Was Promised in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Bram's POV. Five years earlier: a summer regatta, a friendship with Emil Lindqvist, a drunken promise sworn on a broken pocket watch—that if he ever needed leaving, she'd move the hands of the city to do it. Emotional beat: warmth and guilt, the weight of promises made by someone who no longer exists.

chapters.title: The List
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the census bureau, Astrid sees Emil's name on the new registry of enemy nationals slated for deportation within three weeks. She copies it against every rule she swore to uphold. Emotional beat: the first conscious act of treachery toward her own office, justified as family loyalty.

chapters.title: Enemy Blood
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Astrid brings the news to Bram at the observatory. Bram refuses—helping Emil means risking everything she built, including her identity itself. They part angrily. Emotional beat: denial, self-preservation dressed up as prudence.

chapters.title: The Guild's Long Memory
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Master Hessler offers Bram a journeyman's papers—if she completes the master clock flawlessly and stays beyond reproach. Meanwhile a rival apprentice, Kessel, notices Bram's small evasions. Emotional beat: hope dangled like bait, the trap tightening around her double life.

chapters.title: Emil at the Door
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Emil appears at her lodgings at night: dismissed from the harbor, registered, desperate, asking if the old promise still stands. Bram lies and says it doesn't. After he leaves she cannot sleep among her ticking clocks. Emotional beat: shame arriving on schedule, louder than any bell.

chapters.title: Curfew Hours
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid walks the curfewed streets and finds Emil sleeping in the customs shed. She feeds him, argues with him, and realizes he believes Bram will come through—as he always believed in her. Emotional beat: Astrid inheriting faith in a person she barely knows, and resenting it.

chapters.title: The Clock That Keeps the Law
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The city announces the repaired master clock will govern official time: curfews, train departures, patrol rotations. Bram understands the machine she is restoring has become the instrument of Emil's capture. Emotional beat: craftsmanship turned complicit; horror in precision.

chapters.title: An Alliance of Liars
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid confronts Bram at the observatory; they strike a wary bargain—Astrid will delay Emil's file with clerical errors, Bram will find a way to move him. Neither trusts the other yet. Emotional beat: two guarded women signing a contract neither can write down.

chapters.title: Kessel's Curiosity
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Kessel follows Bram to a meeting with Astrid and begins piecing together the truth. Bram buys silence with a rare escapement mechanism, knowing debts to Kessel are never paid once. Emotional beat: paranoia ticking faster than the clocks; the cost of secrets compounding.

chapters.title: The Coal Barge North
chapters.summary: Shared POV alternating scenes. They identify the escape route: a coal barge leaving on the night tide, its captain owed a favor by Emil's old foreman. But the barge departs at 12:40—and after the master clock is certified, patrols will synchronize to it exactly. Emotional beat: the plan forming and the window shrinking in the same breath.

chapters.title: Certification Day
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Before the guild council, Bram demonstrates the perfected master clock; it is flawless. She receives her journeyman's papers and the city's praise. Walking home, she feels nothing but the weight of what the accuracy will cost. Emotional beat: triumph hollowed out; success as sentence.

chapters.title: Astrid's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Her supervisor flags the discrepancies in Emil's file and orders her to correct them personally by week's end. Her loyalty to the bureau, her grief for her parents' respectability, and her promise collide. Emotional beat: the moment loyalty stops being abstract and picks a side.

chapters.title: What Birgitta Owes
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram visits her mother, who never approved of the masquerade, and asks for the old papers proving who she was—to forge Emil's transit documents in their shared surname. Her mother gives them, finally understanding why Bram became someone else. Emotional beat: reconciliation through sacrifice; the past handed over willingly.

chapters.title: Sabotage in Small Parts
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram begins introducing imperceptible errors into the master clock—a drifting minute hand, a lagging strike—errors no inspector would catch for days. Each adjustment feels like breaking her own hands' creed. Emotional beat: a craftsman's agony; love expressed as deliberate imperfection.

chapters.title: Kessel Talks
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Kessel, squeezed by the guild over irregularities, hints to authorities that the census taker and the clockmaker are conspiring. Surveillance begins on the observatory. Emotional beat: the net closing; trust between the two women becoming the only currency left.

chapters.title: The Night Tide
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, climax part one. Escape night: fog, whistles, Emil hidden among coal sacks. Bram must hold the clock's drift just long enough to desynchronize the patrols—but Kessel catches her inside the clock tower. A struggle among the gears; the strike mechanism jams. Emotional beat: terror and resolve fused; the promise kept with her body, not her words.

chapters.title: Midnight, Stopped
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, climax part two. The master clock stops dead at midnight—the whole city hears the silence. Patrols scatter in confusion; the barge slips out on the tide. Astrid arrives to find Bram bleeding beside the arrested Kessel and places herself between Bram and the watch. Emotional beat: the loudest silence in the city; loyalty made public and irreversible.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the inquiry, Astrid testifies that Kessel sabotaged the clock to frame Bram, producing evidence of his extortion. Bram's identity as Birgitta surfaces anyway—but the guild, needing its clockmaker more than its propriety, quietly accepts the fiction going forward. Emotional beat: truth used selectively; survival without absolution.

chapters.title: The Repair
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram rebuilds the master clock honestly, this time keeping it true, and sends word via the barge captain that Emil reached neutral waters. She and Astrid meet at the observatory at midnight to hear twelve bells fall correctly, together. Emotional beat: quiet restoration; a promise fulfilled becoming a future chosen.

chapters.title: Keepers of the Clock
chapters.summary: Alternating final passages, both POVs. Spring: Astrid has left the census bureau to teach; Bram holds journeyman's papers under a name that is now simply hers. In the workshop they hang Emil's broken pocket watch, repaired, above the bench. Emotional beat: belonging not found but built, tick by tick, by two people who chose each other over safety.
